source: Game-owned gearbox catalogue (gearbox swap, 2026-10-13). One row per gearbox file the garage offers. What a physics_sim gearbox file cannot say lives here: display name, kind (manual | sequential | automatic | cvt), focus (economy | touring | performance | race), gear_type (helical | straight_cut, the later gear-whine audio keys on it), synchro (cone | dog), the input torque rating, the dry mass (mass_kg, the gearbox's own node in the garage part-mass tree, rg/part_mass.h; without the differential) and the card text. rating_nm is the maximum engine torque the box is rated for (N*m at the input shaft): physics_sim's GearboxDesc has no rating yet, so the rating is kept HERE and moves into the physics file when the physics session adds one; the garage offers a box only for an engine whose peak torque does not exceed it. All ratings and designs are invented [AS] and chosen to cover the shipped engines (engine peaks: i4 2.0 ~212, A25A 290, N52 300, R26B 608, hyper V8 1387 N*m). Paths are relative to the repository root. The automatic and CVT kinds have no entries yet (physics_sim has no torque converter or variator): the garage lists them as 'coming soon'; the kinds themselves are fixed in rg::GearboxCatalog (gearbox_catalog.h).

gearboxes.name: Economy 5-speed manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a small transverse 5-speed manual without its differential weighs about 28-36 kg (economy cars, recalled, no citation fetched); 32 kg used.
gearboxes.description: Long gearing and a tall overdrive fifth for low engine speed at motorway pace. Light and efficient, built for everyday engines.

gearboxes.name: Economy 6-speed overdrive manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] one more gear pair and a longer case than the 5-speed economy box: 36 kg used, no citation fetched.
gearboxes.description: Two overdrive gears, the sixth very tall. The lowest engine speed on the motorway, at the cost of punch in the top gears.

gearboxes.name: Touring 6-speed manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a mid-size 6-speed manual for 400 N*m (passenger-car class, roughly 35-45 kg dry without differential, recalled, no citation fetched); 40 kg used.
gearboxes.description: The balanced six-speed of the sedans: even steps and a modest overdrive.

gearboxes.name: Close-ratio 6-speed manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] the touring box's size with wider close-ratio gears and stronger synchros: 42 kg used, no citation fetched.
gearboxes.description: Tightly spaced gears keep the engine in its power band after every shift. Short throw, strong synchros, nearly direct sixth.

gearboxes.name: Heavy-duty 6-speed manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a 6-speed rated for 700 N*m (heavy-duty performance class, roughly 48-58 kg dry, recalled, no citation fetched); 52 kg used.
gearboxes.description: Large gears and synchros for high-torque engines. Direct fourth, overdrive fifth and sixth.

gearboxes.name: Hypercar 7-speed manual
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a seven-speed for over 1,500 N*m in a hypercar (dry, its differential is a separate part of the tree): 60-75 kg for boxes of this torque class, recalled, no citation fetched; 68 kg used.
gearboxes.description: The hypercar's seven-speed: a long overdrive seventh for the top speed run and the strength for over 1,500 N*m.

gearboxes.name: Straight-cut 6-speed sequential
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a racing 6-speed sequential dog box with straight-cut gears and a light case for 1,800 N*m: 45-50 kg, recalled, no citation fetched; 48 kg used.
gearboxes.description: Racing dog box with straight-cut gears: no synchros, a sequential drum and very short shifts. Rated for the hypercar.

gearboxes.name: Vintage 3-speed sliding-mesh
gearboxes.mass_source: [AS] a period cast-iron 3-speed sliding-mesh box: 35-40 kg, recalled, no citation fetched; 38 kg used.
gearboxes.description: Three widely spaced straight-cut gears and no synchronisers, as in the earliest motor cars. Match the speeds or it grinds.
